correctness.rationale: For all odd prime powers q and n>=1, augmentation-one reversal invariants are counted as a vector-space hyperplane; equivariant reduction from q[X]/(X^n-1) to q[X]/(X^m-1) has q^((n-m)/2) fibers; the reduced algebra decomposes into fixed roots 1, -1 when present, and paired Frobenius orbits producing independent extension-field norms. The determinant is the product of norms raised to 2*ell^s with an optional -1 eigenvalue. Norm surjectivity gives uniform nonzero values in even orders and uniform nonzero squares in odd non-pure orders; m=1 forces determinant 1. Every boundary including n=1 and characteristic-dividing orders is treated. An independently constructed elimination verifier exhaustively confirms 44 finite cases and all determinant values.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Appel Corollary 1.3 gives surjectivity of determinant on all invertible circulants by varying the value at one fixed root. Fixing that value at 1 removes precisely this freedom. The target determinant can then be forced square in odd order and has an unpaired -1 parameter in even order. The target thus neither repeats nor follows as a numerical corollary of Appel’s stated theorem; the reciprocal decomposition is an additional argument.

value.rationale: The prescribed row-sum-one normalization fixes the constant eigenmode, isolating the determinant obstruction intrinsic to reversible cyclic convolution. This complete arithmetic distribution for all orders and all odd finite fields sharply distinguishes an even-order free unpaired eigenvalue, odd-order square-norm rigidity, and nilpotent pure-characteristic-power degeneration. Exact zero counts and every nonzero fiber form a mathematically motivated infinite classification beyond a routine numeric sample.
